name: Terminal Block-Curvature Tax
statement: Let $\varnothing\ne B\subsetneq A$ be dismantlable ample with $\operatorname{Cor}(A)\subseteq B$. Choose a maximal proper dismantlable-ample intermediate $C$ and put $D=A\setminus C$. Define $\tau(D)=e(D)-|D|+\max\{1,|\operatorname{Cor}(D)|\}$. Then $D$ has minimum graph degree at least two, every cube-family corner of $D$ has a neighbor in $C$, the relative Yang module of $(A,C)$ is deletion-minimal Cohen--Macaulay, and $\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(B)}|S|\ge|A\setminus B|+\tau(D)$. In particular $\tau(D)\ge1$.
proof: Maximality of $C$ excludes every relative teaching concept. Ampleness makes the relative Yang module Cohen--Macaulay, while deleting any $d\in D$ cannot remain ample because then $d$ would be a corner of $A$ outside $C$; the relative Cohen--Macaulay criterion gives deletion-minimality. An isolated residual vertex would teach $C$ by the first edge of an isometric path, and the relative leaf dichotomy similarly excludes residual degree one, so $e(D)\ge|D|$. Every corner of $D$ needs a boundary neighbor in $C$, or its unique maximal cube in $D$ would also make it a corner of $A$. Hence the boundary has at least $\max\{1,|\operatorname{Cor}(D)|\}$ edges. The ample edge--shadow identity converts internal plus boundary edges into the rank sum of newly shattered supports; the earlier supports from $B$ to $C$ each contribute at least one.
